inconsistencies: #35855 and #36233 both bump the Guix time-machine and both claim to close #36232 (native riscv64 Guix builds); they are alternatives, not complements. Review #36233 first (narrower, reproduced hashes, signed ACK) and then decide whether #35855's broader binutils/CMake/lief bump supersedes it.
#36036 (clang 19) also bumps the Xcode CLT minimum to 26.3, which is exactly what the narrower #36287 does. Review #36287 first; #36036 should then be reduced to the clang-only part or rebased on it.
Stack order matters: #36272 (split Guix Linux toolchain) -> #36193 (libstdc++ --disable-wchar_t) -> #25573 (static-pie bitcoind). #36272 must be reviewed first; #25573 states it depends on both.
Compiler-baseline chain: #36042 (g++ 13) and #36287/#36036 (clang/Xcode) are the concrete steps that #36033 (C++23 RFC) needs; reviewing #36033 first would be wasted effort until the baselines land.
#24773 (MSVC SHA256 intrinsics) is in direct tension with #31507 (drop MSVC for clang-cl). The toolchain decision in #31507 should be made first; #24773 becomes redundant if it lands.
#36275 was split out of #36167 and unblocks it, and itself depends on subtree updates #36278/#36298; review #36275 before #36167.
#36269 is stacked on the unmerged #36082; #36082 must be reviewed first.
#36267 consists solely of backports of already-merged master PRs (#36256, #36260); review is verification of the backport, not of the underlying changes.

#35068 and #35765 both fix depends-system handling of native_libmultiprocess (CMake prefix discovery and stale local-source archives respectively) and touch the same area; they are best reviewed together.

#35356 (Windows build dir with spaces) is currently red because of a real path-handling bug in wallet_signer.py; the underlying bug fix belongs to the wallet/test area, and this CI PR cannot be judged until it exists.
result.notes: The category splits cleanly: a small release-integrity/regression head (#36267, #36285, the Guix time-machine and toolchain-stack PRs), a broad P3 middle of CI coverage and build-friction work, and a long P4 tail of warning flags, logging and cosmetic CMake tweaks. Two structural themes generate most of the duplication risk: the Guix time-machine/riscv64 pair and the compiler-minimum-version chain. Several multiprocess/libmultiprocess build PRs (#19460, #32387, #35068, #35454, #35765, #36060) form a loose cluster whose value depends on the wider process-separation project rather than on present build breakage, which is why they sit in P3.
